C ABI + JSON costs one serialisation per call and buys total version independence — and §7.2's document-grained stages exist precisely so "per call" means "per artifact", making that cost invisible. **This is the VST posture the owner asked for:** a plugin compiles ONCE, with any toolchain that can emit a C-ABI cdylib (Rust, C, C++, Zig, Go — authorship is not Rust-bound), and keeps working across vibe releases; migrations happen when OUR plugin API moves (`vibe_ext_abi`, the envelope, `ir_schema` — all versioned, additive within a version, a break announced as a `formats/breaks/` note), never when a compiler does.

facts.ABI-CRATE: vibe ships a small **`vibe-ext` helper crate** (published with the rust stack) so a plugin author writes a safe `fn handle(ctx: Context) -> Reply` and a `vibe_extension!` macro emits the four symbols, the catch_unwind guard, and the (de)serialisation. Authors never touch `unsafe`.
facts.PANIC-AND-VERSION: The loader (libloading) checks `vibe_ext_abi` before any invoke — a mismatch refuses with remediation («rebuild: `vibe build`»), never a crash. Every invoke crosses a catch_unwind at the plugin's own boundary (the macro's job); a panicking plugin fails its execution, reported like any failing contribution — it does not take vibe down.

build-home.title: 8.2 Where native extensions build — in place, amending PROP-024 §2.3

p.IN-SLOT-BUILD: Per the mandate («собирать inplace прямо внутри vibedeps либо внутри packages»), and per the precedent PROP-025 already set (`build_binary` runs `cargo build --release` in the slot): **a dependency's native extension builds inside its own slot** (`<slot>/<crate_dir>` workspace, `target/` in the slot), and an authored package of ours builds inside its `vibevm/vibepacks/...` live slot with its own workspace. This AMENDS PROP-024 §2.3's «build output is directed to a gitignored location e.g. `.vibe/<pkg>-target/`, never the slot» — the amendment is recorded here and lands at that anchor at build time: build output in the slot was already reality for PROP-025 binaries, it stays outside the content hash and the shippable tree by the §2.2 denylist (`target/`, `node_modules/`), and what makes it SAFE is §9 (materialisation stops deleting what it did not write). vibe maintains the ignore entries (a generated `.gitignore` inside the vibedeps root covering `**/target/` and `**/node_modules/` — the vendored world stays clean in git without per-slot files).

p.BUILD-PHASE-OWNS-IT: The **build phase** builds native extensions (and `[[binary]]`s) — with cargo's own incrementality and `vibe bin build`'s narration genre (announced per artifact; PROP-025's build-consent prompt dies with the rest of the prompts, `##INSTALL-IS-CONSENT` — that amendment rides §9's plan too). Lazily building on first use stays available for `binary` handlers (as today); `native` handlers used by the COMPILER are never built lazily mid-compile — see the bootstrap order.

p.PREBUILT-CLOSED: **Closed-source plugins ship prebuilt** (owner case 2026-08-25): a package may carry ready cdylib artifacts instead of (or beside) sources — `handler = { kind = "native", prebuilt = { "windows-x86_64" = "ext/bin/squeeze.dll", "linux-x86_64" = "ext/bin/libsqueeze.so", "macos-aarch64" = "ext/bin/libsqueeze.dylib" } }`, keyed by the PROP-000 platform trio's target names. A prebuilt artifact is ordinary package content: hashed into `content_hash`, materialised verbatim, integrity for free. Loading order: prebuilt for the current platform if declared, else build from `crate_dir` if sources ship, else refuse naming the missing platform — never a silent skip. The build phase skips prebuilt-only natives (nothing to build); `vibe_ext_abi`/`ir_schema` gates apply to a prebuilt exactly as to a built one, which is what makes closed-source distribution SAFE to version: the C-ABI wire (§8.1) is the whole contract, so one artifact per platform serves every vibe release the schema allows.

p.BOOTSTRAP-ORDER: **The bootstrap order, stated because install precedes build:** if an activated `compile:` transform's cdylib artifact is absent when install compiles the lane, install compiles WITHOUT it, marks the lane `transforms-pending` in the artifact header, and says so; the build phase, having built the extension, re-runs the (cheap) lane compile so the chain `vibe build` converges in one invocation. A `vibe install` alone with a missing transform artifact is thus honest and usable, never wedged — and never silently different from what the manifest declares.

p.WASM-DEFERRED: **WASM handlers — deferred, not rejected:** a wasm component would buy sandboxing (the PROP-020 §4 accepted-risk posture could tighten) and cross-platform artifacts, at the cost of a runtime dependency and awkward filesystem/process access — exactly the operations phase handlers exist to do. When the sandboxing need fires (third-party plugin ecosystems beyond the allow-list), this anchor is where the design resumes. Until then the trust gate is the boundary, exactly as PROP-020 records it.

compile-native-only.title: 8.5 Why compile: takes only builtin and native

p.COMPILE-NATIVE-ONLY: A `compile:` transform runs on every lane regeneration — inside install, potentially per document. A process spawn per document (script/binary kinds) is a Windows-hostile cost multiplier and an interpreter-availability hazard inside the innermost loop the whole product depends on; and an agent in the compiler would make the boot lane non-deterministic, which PROP-009 forbids constitutionally. Hence: `builtin` and `native` only — the two in-process kinds.

incremental.title: 9. The incremental-install revision — materialise becomes a diff

problem.title: 9.1 The defect, named from the code

p.WIPE-TODAY: Today `materialise_with` (vibe-workspace `vibedeps.rs`) clears the whole slot (`remove_dir_all`) and re-copies on every re-materialisation, and a **mutable local source is NEVER presence-trusted** (`install.rs`: `!dep.source_mutable` in the trust gate) — so every `vibe install` over an edited-in-workspace package wipes its slot, and with it the `target/` PROP-025 just built there. The owner's fear is already a live defect for package binaries; native compile («может идти очень долго») raises the stakes, it does not create them.

p.MATERIALISE-CODE-MAP: **Where materialisation lives TODAY** (verified 2026-08-24/25): the copy machine — `crates/vibe-workspace/src/vibedeps.rs` (`materialise` / `materialise_with` — the `remove_dir_all` + `copy_tree` pair this section replaces with a diff; `slot_rel_path`/`slot_abs_path`; the returned footprint `Vec<PathBuf>` this section's record persists); the transformed-slot variant — `vibedeps/derived.rs` (`materialise_with_spec_format`, the `.vibe-derived.toml` manifest §9.2 absorbs, `LEGACY0_EXCLUDES`); the trust gate and per-dep loop — `install.rs` (`materialise_resolution_with_spec_format`: the `present`/`format_current`/`!dep.source_mutable`/`slot_integrity` decision, `SlotIntegrity::TrustPresence|Verify`, the `slot_verifier` seam); freshness — `freshness.rs` (`hold_pins` and the fresh-check the install verb consults); hooks that must re-run only on real change — `hooks.rs` + `install/hooks_run.rs`; the in-slot binary precedent — `bins.rs` (`build_binary`, `DeclaredBinary::artifact`).

record.title: 9.2 The slot record — the footprint becomes a file

p.SLOT-RECORD: Every materialised slot gains a **slot record** — `.vibe-slot.toml` at the slot root: schema, the source `content_hash`, the spec-format identity (absorbing PROP-045's `.vibe-derived.toml` fields for transformed slots — ONE record file, not two), and `[[file]]` rows `{path, sha256}` for every file the materialiser wrote. `materialise` already returns exactly this footprint («and, in a later phase, record» — its own docstring names this phase); the record is that promise kept. The record itself, like the derived manifest today, is outside the content hash.

diff.title: 9.3 The diff algorithm — write what changed, delete what was ours, touch nothing else

p.DIFF-MATERIALISE: Re-materialising a slot that carries a record: **(1)** compute the incoming footprint (path→hash) from the source; **(2)** for each incoming file — recorded hash equal ⇒ **leave the file untouched** (no write, no mtime change); differing or unrecorded ⇒ write it; **(3)** for each RECORDED file absent from the incoming footprint ⇒ delete it (and now-empty parent dirs, best-effort); **(4)** any on-disk path NOT in the record — `target/`, `node_modules/`, any build output — is **never touched**; **(5)** write the new record. A slot with no record (legacy) pays one last full wipe-and-copy and comes out recorded. `vibe clean` remains the only whole-slot wipe (PROP-053 unchanged).

facts.MTIME-LAW: **Step 2's "untouched" is a law, not an optimisation:** unchanged files keep their bytes AND their mtimes, so cargo's fingerprinting sees an unchanged workspace and the native/binary rebuild inside the slot is a no-op. This single property is what makes «инкрементальность — супер важный кусок» hold end-to-end: edit one prompt file in a package → one file rewritten in the slot → cargo rebuilds nothing.
facts.MUTABLE-GETS-A-GATE: **Mutable sources get a freshness gate instead of a wipe:** for a PROP-011 §2.6 `file://` working-tree source, install re-hashes the source's shippable tree (cheap — read-and-hash, no copy) and compares against the record's `content_hash`: equal ⇒ the slot is fresh, skip entirely (this is the missing half of «vibe.toml не поменялся — не инсталлировать»); differing ⇒ the §9.3 diff. The never-trust-presence rule stays true in spirit — presence alone is still not trusted; the record's hash is what earns the skip.
facts.SELF-HEAL: **Drift repair gets cheaper, not weaker.** PROP-020's reset guarantee (hook edits never compound) is re-based: "reset" = the §9.3 diff restores every RECORDED file to footprint state, byte-exact, whenever the slot re-materialises; `verify`-integrity mode compares per-file against the record and heals only divergent files. Hooks re-run only when the diff actually changed something — re-running them over an untouched slot would compound effects, the exact disease PROP-020 §2.1 exists to prevent.
facts.AMENDMENT-PLAN: **Amendments this section obligates at build time** (recorded here so the build session lands them at the owning anchors, statuses moved, nothing renamed): PROP-011 gains the diff-materialise ruling and the mutable-source freshness gate; PROP-020 §2.1 `##RESET-THEN-RERUN` gains the record-diff-restore successor note, and its §2.3 trust gate (allow-list, first-run consent, non-interactive abort, `--allow-hooks`) is superseded by `##INSTALL-IS-CONSENT` + §3.5 observability; PROP-022 §2.2's snapshot reset language likewise; PROP-045's manifest is absorbed into the slot record (its facts re-pointed, file format superseded); PROP-024 §2.3 per §8.2; PROP-025's build-consent prompt likewise yields to `##INSTALL-IS-CONSENT`.

p.TEST-LOG-PLUGIN: A fixture package declares in its own manifest: `[[extension]] id="announce" point="phase:build" handler={kind="builtin", name="log"} config={message="hello from {phase} in {project}"}` (plus a second execution at `phase:test` — the multi-execution property under test). E2E: install the fixture into a scratch project, run `vibe test`, assert stdout carries both rendered lines in phase order, each attributed to the providing package (§3.3 surface rule); run `vibe test` again and assert the executions report `fresh` (§4.3 under test); assert `vibe extensions --json` lists both executions with their provider (§3.5 under test), and that a host `[extensions] disable = [...]` line silences exactly one of them (§3.3 under test). The `log` builtin renders `{phase}`, `{project}`, `{package}` from the envelope — proving the envelope reaches handlers, which is the scenario's real point.

compiler-test.title: 10.2 Compiler: the XML whitespace squeezer — a TEST vehicle, not a shipping practice

p.TEST-XML-MINIFY: A `compile:emitted` transform (builtin first — proving the declaration/activation/ordering tract; then re-shipped as a `native` cdylib in a fixture package — proving the §8 build/load/invoke tract with byte-identical output, which is itself the assertion). **The algorithm, XML-aware and safe by parent-shape:** parse the emitted XML; delete every text node consisting solely of whitespace whose parent element has at least one ELEMENT child and no non-whitespace text child (pure element containers lose their pretty-printing; mixed-content elements — anything carrying prose — are untouched byte-for-byte); comments (the compiled lane's `vibe:` markers) and CDATA survive verbatim; serialise. Applies to `.xml` artifacts only.

p.MINIFY-NOT-FOR-PROD: **The owner's own caveat, recorded as a norm:** inter-tag whitespace stripping is a poor production idea — token savings are marginal and the readability/diffability of the lane (and its reversibility oracle, §7.3) suffer. The transform ships as a test fixture and a mechanics-proof, default-off everywhere; the real tenant of these stages is the future **Caveman compression** pass at `compile:lane`, which compresses prose content deliberately rather than shaving markup accidentally.

facts.REJ-TWO-GRAMMARS: **Two separate extension grammars** (a `[hooks]`-style table for lifecycle, a Babel-style list for the compiler) — rejected: the mandate's core is one coherent machine; divergence here is the «разброд» the owner named as the failure mode.
facts.REJ-FULL-MAVEN-PHASES: **Adopting Maven's full 23-phase table** — rejected: the hyphenated phases exist to sequence JVM build minutiae we do not have; nine phases cover the mandate, and the phase table is extensible behind a ruling when a real between-slot need arrives.
facts.REJ-RUST-ABI: **`dylib` with Rust-native symbols** (handing `&mut DocTree` across the boundary) — rejected: no stable Rust ABI exists; every plugin would be pinned to the exact compiler and vibe build, which is undistributable. C ABI + JSON (§8.1) is the only honest wire.
facts.REJ-SUBPROCESS-COMPILER: **Script/binary handlers for `compile:` stages** — rejected (§8.5): spawn-per-document inside install's innermost loop, interpreter availability as a compile dependency, and agent handlers there would break boot-lane determinism.
facts.REJ-CLOSURE-HOOKS: **Closure/graph access in the STAGED tier** (a tier-1 transform adding/removing `#use` edges) — rejected as a prompt-injection lever and an auditability break (§7.2 `##NO-CLOSURE-HOOK`). Full access moved tiers rather than dying: the 2026-08-25 ruling prices it into the pass tier behind `compiler_internals` + host activation + the header record (§7.4.3) — an explicit capability, never a silent one.
facts.DEFER-HANDLE-API: **Deferred: an interactive handle/callback C API for passes** (the LLVM-C-API genre — the plugin calls back into vibe to walk and mutate nodes piecemeal) — the pass wire is whole-IR-in/whole-IR-out (§7.4.4) until a real pass demonstrably cannot be written that way; the deferral lives behind this anchor.
facts.REJ-INLINE-COMMANDS-STAND: **Inline command strings in the manifest** — stays rejected exactly as PROP-020 §3 ruled; the `script` kind keeps the reviewable-file form, and `builtin`/`binary`/`native` are the structured alternatives.
facts.DEFER-GOAL-MIXING: **Deferred:** direct-verb mixing in a chain (`##EXISTING-VERBS-STAY`); WASM handlers (`##WASM-DEFERRED`); a per-node visitor API for external transforms (`##NOT-FROM-BABEL`); pkgrefs scoping non-install phases (`##CHAIN-GENERAL`).

roadmap.title: 12. The proposed build order — six self-standing waves

facts.R1-DIFF: **R1 — the materialise diff (§9).** Slot record, diff algorithm, mutable-source freshness gate, mtime law; amendments landed at PROP-011/020/022/024/045 anchors. Ships alone and pays immediately: `vibe install` stops killing slot `target/`s (a today-bug for PROP-025 binaries), and edit-one-prompt installs become near-instant. **First because everything after it builds artifacts the old wipe would destroy.**
facts.R2-ENGINE: **R2 — the lifecycle engine (§3–§6 minus agent).** The phase table, chain grammar (superseding PROP-053 `##CHAIN-ONLY-INSTALL` at its anchor), `[[extension]]` parsing, trust-gate extension, envelope, `builtin`/`script`/`binary` handlers, `.vibe/lifecycle.toml` freshness, the `log` builtin, and the §10.1 e2e. `vibe build`/`vibe test` become real (preset: binaries + stack commands).
facts.R3-IR-REFACTOR: **R3 — the IR refactor (§7.5).** Explicit level types, built-in phases as named passes, the declared default pipeline, the inter-pass verifier skeleton — no external API yet. Gate: byte-identical artifacts over the whole corpus, judged by the existing oracles. Before both compiler tiers, so they are born on the pass manager instead of retrofitted onto the monolith.
facts.R4-STAGED: **R4 — tier 1, the staged transforms (§7.2).** The four canonical transform positions, host activation, the transforms header, the oracle rule, and the §10.2 builtin minifier e2e.
facts.R5-NATIVE: **R5 — the native tier (§8).** `vibe-ext` crate, the four-symbol ABI, loader + catch_unwind + version gate, build-phase integration, bootstrap order, and the §10.2 native-parity e2e.
facts.R6-PASS-TIER: **R6 — tier 2, the pass tier (§7.4).** The `compiler_internals` flag, pass declarations (transform/lowering/frontend/backend), the whole-IR wire with `ir_schema`, the verifier turned on between plugin passes, `vibe list`/`show` surfacing. E2E: a fixture frontend for a trivial format whose documents resolve as `spec://` citizens, and a fixture JSON backend for the lane — both behind the flag, both refused without it.
facts.R7-AGENT: **R7 — create and the agent tier (§6.4–§6.5).** The real provider seam, selected-world agent execution, strict multi-output result, durable hosted outbox/fingerprint resume and shared CLI/MCP lifecycle surfaces are complete through the all-green R7.4 boundary. Provider presence activates nothing and hosted work spends nothing.
facts.R7-EXTERNAL-ORCHESTRATION: **R7.5 — neutral external orchestration mechanics (§4.6).** P0 fixes the evidence/optional-provider/vocabulary laws; P1 adds JTD-first input/artifact/run evidence; P2 builds the read-only `vibe-specdoc` authoring + `vibe-facts` consumer projection with optional current/carried specmap relations; P3 exposes one thin requirements query over CLI/MCP and proves it beside existing lifecycle control with a fake external PDSA process. No coding agent, automatic repair loop, task-choice heuristic or Plan/Act policy is implemented; a reference agent remains a separate future campaign.
facts.R8-PACKAGE-DEPLOY: **R8 — package/deploy substance.** Skill/plugin/installer bindings for package; first deploy plugins. Shaped by what exists when its turn comes; deliberately last.

facts.OPEN-PHASE-NAMES: **Naming — CLOSED (owner, 2026-08-25: «окей»):** the nine-phase table stands as drafted — `generate` separate from `build`, `verify` in the table from day one, the name `create` confirmed.
facts.OPEN-NATIVE-TRUST: **Native trust — CLOSED (owner, 2026-08-25):** no consent tier of any kind — installation is the consent (`##INSTALL-IS-CONSENT`), for in-process cdylibs exactly as for scripts, the Gradle/Webpack/Clang norm. The safety budget is spent on §3.5 observability. §8.3's wasm sandboxing note stays the eventual escape if a hostile-ecosystem era ever demands one.
facts.OPEN-CREATE-BUDGET: **Create economics — CLOSED (owner, 2026-08-26):** there is no one global create budget. `##LLM-BUDGET` defines per-enhancement/per-workload call and token ceilings, lazy spend and mode-specific exhaustion. Exact defaults/manifest grammar remain implementation work at the first consuming enhancement; the policy fork is closed.
facts.OPEN-DEPLOY-TARGETS: **Deploy first targets — CLOSED (owner, 2026-08-26):** selected genres are project/user agent projections for Claude Code, Codex and OpenCode; VibeVM-owned local tools under `~/.vibe/bin`; an explicit custom installer for ordinary applications; registry/marketplace/server/remote providers; and future system-scope package/config/service providers. The first commissioning cut is isolated local projection/`vibe-bin`, never a live publish/server mutation. Runtime target/provider statuses remain R8 work at their own anchors.

p.REF-LIFECYCLE-TOML: Machine state: inside `.vibe/` (shippable-tree denylist), never committed, never hashed, survives `vibe clean` (§4.3), erasable at will — losing it costs one full re-run, nothing else. Schema-versioned like every state file we own.

slot-record.title: 14.3 .vibe-slot.toml — the materialised-slot record (§9.2)
slot-record.fence:
schema = 1 source_hash = "sha256:…" # content_hash of the shippable tree that was materialised spec_format = "xml" # mixed | markdown | xml — absorbs .vibe-derived.toml's role converter_recipe = "…" # present iff transformed (PROP-045 genre) derived_hash = "sha256:…" # present iff transformed overlay_hash = "sha256:…" # present iff a facts overlay applied
[[file]] # one row per file the MATERIALISER wrote — the footprint path = "vibevm/vibespecs/boot/20-stack.md" # slot-relative, forward-slashed, sorted sha256 = "…" # for transformed slots rows also carry: source = "…", disposition = "converted"|"copied"

p.REF-SLOT-RECORD: Lives at the slot root; excluded from the slot's content identity exactly as `.vibe-derived.toml` is today; unknown fields refuse (deny_unknown, schema bump to extend). The §9.3 diff reads the old record, computes the incoming footprint, and writes the new record LAST — a crash between steps leaves a slot the next run heals (recorded files re-diff; unrecorded paths were never touched).

facts.REF-WIRE-SCRIPT: **script:** interpreter per PROP-020 §2.2 (`.sh` via bash first, `.ps1` via PowerShell on Windows fallback); cwd = slot for `slot:` points, project root for `phase:`; env = the `VIBE_*` set PROP-020 documents plus `VIBE_CONTEXT` (absolute path of the envelope JSON written into scratch) and `VIBE_REPLY` (absolute path where a reply JSON MAY be written); exit 0 + no reply file = `{"status":"ok"}`; non-zero exit = fail regardless of reply file; streams go to the user live.
facts.REF-WIRE-BINARY: **binary:** the artifact is resolved via PROP-025 (`DeclaredBinary::artifact`, built if absent); envelope JSON on stdin (closed after write); reply JSON expected on stdout (whole stdout parsed as one JSON document; stderr streams to the user); non-zero exit = fail; a malformed reply = fail naming the execution.
facts.REF-WIRE-NATIVE: **native, one invocation, seven steps:** (1) resolve artifact — prebuilt-for-platform, else built cdylib, else refuse; (2) load (libloading), once per run, cached by path; (3) `vibe_ext_abi()` — must equal a supported ABI version or refuse with «rebuild: vibe build»; (4) `vibe_ext_manifest()` — parse, check the execution's id/point/`ir_schema` are declared; (5) `vibe_ext_invoke(req, req_len, &resp, &resp_len)` under `catch_unwind` at the plugin macro's boundary — request/response are UTF-8 JSON byte buffers, envelope in, reply out; non-zero return or panic = the execution fails, vibe survives; (6) parse reply; (7) `vibe_ext_free(resp, resp_len)`. The `vibe-ext` helper crate's `vibe_extension!` macro generates all four symbols from a safe `fn handle(Context) -> Reply`.

agent-wire.title: 14.5 The agent handshake, on the wire (§6.5)
agent-wire.fence:
# .vibe/agentic/outbox/<run-id>/<execution-id>.md — one task file per agent execution --- run: "<run-id>" execution: "org.vibevm.x/y#draft-guide" phase: "create" outputs: # the contract vibe validates on resume - path: "docs/guide.md" accept: "non-empty file" --- <the resolved prompt document, then the envelope's prose projection>
# printed to stdout, then the phase exits with status `delegated`: ```vibe-agent-tasks run: <run-id> tasks: - .vibe/agentic/outbox/<run-id>/draft-guide.md resume: vibe <requested-phase> ```

p.REF-AGENT-RESUME: Resume is the SAME phase command re-run: the engine adopts the exact `run_id` in `.vibe/lifecycle.toml` (engine status `delegated`), validates each task's declared outputs, marks satisfied executions done, re-parks unsatisfied ones (idempotent), and continues the chain. A fresh/displacing identity never services that run's continuation. No dedicated resume verb; the default-lifecycle command's lifecycle `--force` deliberately displaces/re-parks (not Reinstall's unrelated materialisation `--force`, which may adopt the same run). Repetition beyond that one state transition belongs to an external orchestrator, never a hidden coding-agent loop (§4.6).

ir-skeletons.title: 14.6 IR level skeletons (tier-2 wire; frozen at R6, sketched now)

p.REF-IR-UNFROZEN: These skeletons fix the VOCABULARY (level names, the node/edge/entry framing); exact field sets freeze in R6 when the wire ships, derived from the R3 types — deliberately, so the refactor is not forced to mirror a JSON guess made before it ran. `ir_schema` starts at 1 the day the first external pass can load.

external-orchestration-wire.title: 14.7 R7.5 evidence and requirements wires

p.REF-EVIDENCE-WIRE: P1 freezes the following vocabulary as strict JTD and registers/corpora/code-generates it before runtime use. `observed_at` is excluded from `evidence_id`; the id is a domain-separated digest over every other canonical identity/comparison member. `measured` values come from durable execution state; `observed` values are recomputed at verify. Optional members are absent, never `null`.

p.REF-REQUIREMENTS-WIRE: P1 also freezes one strict metadata-only requirements report. It does not embed verification evidence into fact rows: the lifecycle evidence member and the fact/relation observations are independent roots an external orchestrator may join by full address/edge and exact observation identity.

p.REF-REQUIREMENTS-SURFACES: The shared library query is projected as `vibe requirements [--address-prefix <spec://prefix>] [--limit <N>] [--relations] [--json] [--path <project>]` and MCP `requirements_query({address_prefix?, limit?, relations?})`. Default limit is 100, hard maximum 256; zero, overflow, wrong types and unknown members refuse before filesystem access. MCP has no path member because server context is authority. With `relations = false` no specmap engine/map is loaded. Existing `vibe verify --json` and `lifecycle_run({phase:"verify"})` are the control/evidence surfaces; R7.5 adds no second lifecycle executor and no `evidence` verb merely to duplicate their generated root.
